extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD contracting officers, contract negotiators, and acquisition personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for Contracting Officers implementing Commercial/Industrial Type Activities (CITA) service procurements, including milestone planning, Statement of Work preparation, cost-comparison notices/clauses, and maintaining procurement integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Office responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepares Government Cost Estimate. Conducts Cost Comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned role in the acquisition/cost-comparison cycle; part of the Task Group supporting preparation and comparison of government in-house costs with contractor offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Office responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews SOW and solicitation for legal sufficiency. Assists in responses to requests under the Freedom of Information Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal office must ensure the SOW and solicitation are legally defensible and support FOIA responses as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Office core duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Assures contracting milestones are met; reviews work specifications; solicits bids/offers from private industry; conducts pre-bid or proposal conferences; explains cost procedures; presides at bid openings and determines successful responsive/responsible bids or acceptable/responsible offers; awards contracts; notifies appropriate activity officials when a contract is actually awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Office should be engaged in planning and specification development; failure to be sufficiently involved risks poorly prepared SOWs and ill-defined milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer early involvement in planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer should be significantly involved, at least initially, in development of specifications and milestone planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early participation helps produce usable SOWs, realistic milestone schedules, and maintains integrity of competitive bidding; attendance at initial Task Group planning meetings is encouraged even if continual attendance is impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone planning analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully analyze input to milestone planning to ensure the Contracting Officer can perform in accordance with the resulting schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess issues such as negotiation time, SBA coordination, auditing of cost/pricing data, need for clear SOWs; recognize that entire procurement cycle may take several months and that adherence to milestones depends on SOW condition and sound planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation method selection and timeline impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of solicitation (formal advertising, Two-Step Formal Advertising, negotiated including 8(a) set-asides) materially affects procurement time and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally advertised procedures (including small business restricted advertising) are usually quickest because they do not require submission/evaluation of technical proposals or extensive cost data; Two-Step increases time due to technical proposal evaluation prior to priced bids; negotiated/8(a) procurements typically require cost/pricing data, audits, and negotiations and are generally the longest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award clearances and surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be necessary to conduct pre-award surveys or obtain security or Equal Employment Opportunity clearances prior to award of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security clearances for contractors can be a major delay (often up to 60 days; interim clearances may take ~30 days); include these requirements in milestone estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) must be performance-oriented and equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: SOW must be written around the same scope of work and same level of performance regardless of who performs the work, the Government or the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular A-76 ground rule: SOW should not advantage one performer over another; must provide common basis for cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOW precision and avoidance of misinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The work statement must be sufficiently precise to avoid misinterpretation by the contractor with performance standards that can be monitored for either in-house or contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous or imprecise SOWs lead to poor contractor performance recourse and enforcement difficulties; if SOW lacks precision, Contracting Officer may need to rewrite it before solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOW should state what, not how
rubrics_metrics.description: SOW should clearly indicate what is to be done without describing how to do it, and should provide methods of evaluating performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prescribing methods or organization; focus on required outcomes and measurable performance criteria that apply equally to government and contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOW content requirements (duties, tasks, facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: SOW should describe all duties, tasks, responsibilities, and requirements for furnishing facilities and materials; identify government-furnished facilities, materials, and equipment if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When workload is variable, estimates should be based on historical data and best estimates of future requirements; maximum use should be made of contractor facilities where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOW and surveillance plan linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the SOW and the surveillance plan go hand-in-hand: desired performance levels, methods of assessing performance, and criteria to determine acceptable or deficient performance are key ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A surveillance/monitoring plan should accompany the SOW so contractor performance can be assessed against objective criteria; lack of surveillance plans was identified as a common deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanding Officer certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanding Officer must certify that the cost comparison process will be based on the most efficient organization for in-house operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOWs based only on existing position descriptions may not satisfy this requirement; certification ensures in-house cost estimate reflects an efficient organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity and equitable treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for equitable and consistent treatment of all interested persons, groups, and organizations; maintain overall integrity and avoid even the appearance of compromise in the competitive bidding system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrity is a primary objective; violations or appearances of compromise can lead to severe criticism; take precautions to prevent leak or misuse of cost data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding in-house cost estimate access
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel involved in contracting and evaluation should have no access to the Government in-house cost estimate until the most favorable offer to the Government has been determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the number of personnel with access; failure to safeguard has occurred in practice and can compromise the process; require signatures on Standards of Conduct statements and task-group procedures to ensure objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group standards of conduct and chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Task Group members should review and sign Standards of Conduct statements and the Task Group Chairperson must advise members of the importance of maintaining integrity and objectivity and establish procedures to assure this is accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air Force practice cited as example; Contracting Officer may assist or take initiative to implement similar measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Notice of Cost Comparison — formally advertised solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation provision must notify bidders that solicitation is subject to a Government cost comparison; bidders and the union will be provided the in-house cost estimate for review at bid opening or as soon as practicable; other interested parties may request a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government in-house estimate compared with low responsive/responsible bidder; contract award not made for at least five workdays after bid opening to allow review; three-year cost comparison methodology applies (straightline bids/costs for missing years; adjust only known changes excluding inflation); copies of completed cost comparison made available after award or cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Notice of Cost Comparison — negotiated solicitations / 8(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government in-house cost estimate shall be submitted in a sealed envelope prior to the closing time for priced proposals; at conclusion of negotiations and after the most favorable offer is determined, the Contracting Officer will set time/place for public opening of the in-house estimate and notify interested parties; the in-house estimate is considered a "proposal" for Late Proposals rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract award not made for at least five workdays after opening of the in-house estimate; appeals regarding cost comparison data must be submitted in writing within the five-day work period after opening; cost comparison based on three-year projections; if in-house estimate is lower, solicitation shall be canceled; copies of completed cost comparison made available upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of required contract clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations must include clauses relating to equal employment opportunity, veterans preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits (including OFPP Policy Letter No. 78-2 on "wage busting"), and a clause requiring contractor to give displaced employees right of refusal for employment openings for which they may be qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clauses are required by the Circular and other guidance and normally appear in most service contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible/locally-developed protective clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities have developed local clauses such as cooperation with successor contractors during turnover/phase-in; requiring a strike contingency plan; price reduction for nonavailability of operational assets or substandard performance; unbalanced bid evaluation clause to declare bids non-responsive if buy-in appears likely; requirement that contractor use same number of personnel as proposed in Step One of Two-Step Formal Advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legality/enforceability of some local clauses may be questionable; in the absence of specific DAR coverage, Contracting Officers often insert clauses they deem necessary to protect government interests and equity of the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAR coverage and clause consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense Acquisition Regulation (DAR) guidance on service contracting is sparse and spread piece-meal, leading to proliferation of clause variations among agencies and field activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fragmentation has produced at least six different variations of the cost comparison clause in reviewed directives/solicitations/contracts; Contracting Officers should be aware of inconsistent coverage and the need for standardized clause usage where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-aside handling and 8(a) procedural special treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD/Navy directives encourage use of small and disadvantaged businesses, but procedures for 8(a) set-asides are complex; guidance indicates 8(a) actions in excess of $100,000 will be offered up for 8(a) and small business set-asides and firm/bid procedures will apply; SBA development monies will not be included in cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confusion existed about whether set-aside procedures that result in lower in-house cost obviate the need for unrestricted solicitation; CNM guidance (Aug 1979) said 8(a) procurements require further solicitation under Small Business Restricted Advertising or unrestricted solicitation if in-house estimate is lower, whereas competitive small business set-asides would not require further solicitation if in-house cost is lower; in 8(a) cases the Government estimate will be opened but not made public unless the 8(a) offer is lower.
